claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of the official UK government guidance, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**The main issue is that you do not live in the UK.** This is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility. According to the official guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit only if you live in the UK.

While you meet several other important requirements:
- ✓ Alex is 13 years old (under 16)
- ✓ You contribute £26.05/week towards Alex's upkeep, which meets or exceeds the Child Benefit amount
- ✓ Alex is not in care, not working 24+ hours/week, and has no other disqualifying circumstances

The UK residence requirement is essential. There are only limited exceptions to this rule, such as:
- Living in certain specific countries covered by reciprocal agreements
- Being a Crown servant posted abroad

Unless you fall into one of these exceptional categories, you cannot claim Child Benefit while living outside the UK, regardless of how well you support your child financially.

If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK, you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex, provided you continue to contribute adequately to their upkeep.

reasonings: Alex is 13 years old (under 16), which meets the age requirement for Child Benefit. Alex does not live with the claimant, but the claimant contributes £26.05/week towards Alex's upkeep. According to the guidance on 'Child Benefit if your child lives with someone else', if the child lives with someone else and you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards their upkeep, you can continue to receive Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks. The claimant's contribution of £26.05/week meets or exceeds the Child Benefit rate, which would normally allow eligibility in this situation. However, the critical disqualifying factor is that the claimant does not live in the UK. According to the main eligibility page, you 'normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK.' The guidance states you may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant, but without evidence that the claimant falls into one of these exceptions, the requirement to live in the UK is not met. Therefore, despite meeting other criteria (child's age, sufficient contributions, no disqualifying circumstances for the child), the claimant is INELIGIBLE due to not residing in the UK.
